raw_response:
Alright, twenty-five years on this same five mu. My husband picks up construction work in town when he can, the two kids are still in school, so most of the field work falls on me. Five mu isn't enough to live on by itself — that's why he goes out for wages — but the wheat and maize together keep grain in the house and a bit to sell.

Here's how I'm thinking about this year.

**Wheat first.** I'll get it in around early October, right after the maize comes off. I buy seed from the supply shop in town — I stopped saving my own years ago, the new varieties yield more. About 8 kg per mu, maybe 30 yuan worth.

Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind. One bag is 50 kg, costs about 200 yuan. Five bags for my five mu, that's a thousand yuan gone right there. It hurts but everyone says you need a good base or the wheat won't tiller properly.

In spring when the wheat greens up (返青) I topdress urea — about 15 kg per mu, half a bag. Old Wang next door says to spread it just before irrigating so the water carries it down. He's been right about most things.

I water three times — once before winter so it doesn't dry out, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. The well is shared with two other households so we take turns. Maybe 30 yuan per mu each watering for electricity. Spray herbicide once after the wheat is up, and last year I had to spray for aphids too.

I hire a small tractor for plowing in the fall, about 50 yuan per mu, and the combine at harvest, 60 yuan per mu. Can't do those by hand anymore — back won't take it.

I figure on about 400 kg per mu. Last year was 420, the year before only 380 because spring was so dry. Some neighbors pull 500 but their land is better and they spread more fertilizer than I can afford.

**Then maize, straight after wheat harvest in June.** This part is the stressful one — I have to get the wheat off and the maize in within about a week or the season's too short. I buy hybrid seed, the Zhengdan kind usually, around 60 yuan per mu.

For maize I put less down at planting — half a bag of compound per mu, about 30 kg. Then at the big-bell stage (大喇叭口期) I topdress 20 kg of urea per mu. Maize grows fast and we usually get rain in July-August so I only irrigate once, maybe twice if it's dry at silking.

Spray herbicide once after planting, watch for corn borer. Combine at harvest like the wheat.

Yield should be around 450 kg per mu. Last year was 470.

Total input cost for the year, around 4,400 yuan. With grain prices like last year I'll clear maybe 5-6 thousand after expenses. That's why my husband still goes to town.
